queens.observations: Significant warmup effect: first run is 18x slower than average of subsequent runs. Standard deviation is high due to first run outlier.

sieve.observations: First run shows warmup effect (2.4x slower than minimum). After warmup, performance is relatively stable with occasional outlier (run 6: 346183us).

towers.observations: Strong warmup effect: first run is 4.5x slower, second run is 3x slower. Performance stabilizes from run 3 onwards with minimal variance.

permute.observations: Extreme warmup effect: first run is 112x slower than subsequent runs. After warmup, performance is very stable (1-3ms range).

list.observations: Significant warmup effect: first run is 3.3x slower, second run is 1.9x slower. After warmup (run 3+), performance is very stable with only 5% variance.

overall_observations: All benchmarks show significant JIT warmup effects with first run 2-112x slower
Performance stabilizes after 2-3 runs in most benchmarks
Permute has the most extreme warmup effect (112x)
After warmup, benchmarks show good stability (5-10% variance)
Queens and permute are fastest (sub-20ms stable), sieve is slowest (240ms stable)
